title: Coverage audit
description: Which acceptance criteria the tests prove, one entry per criterion. There is deliberately no percentage, ratio, or score anywhere in this contract: docs/concepts/assertion.md holds that coverage is observability and that no gate, threshold, or acceptance criterion may be expressed as a coverage figure, because a number that must rise becomes a target to satisfy and satisfying it produces tests nobody needed. Naming the criteria is what a reader cannot recover from a number. The artifact carries no severity and no verdict — the agent this comes from graded each gap and fed the grade to an approval gate, which is foundation/0005 R5's choosing what runs next.

contract_version.description: A consumer rejects an artifact it was not built to read rather than inferring version from shape.

audit_id.description: Stable identifier for this audit, supplied by the caller and never minted by the producer.

producer.description: What performed the audit. Not a const: the contract requires the artifact, not a particular producer of it.

test_files.description: Every path searched for covering tests. Required so an `uncovered` entry states what it was uncovered against: a criterion proven in a file nobody searched is a false gap.

entries.description: One entry per criterion supplied, sorted by criterion identifier. Omitting a criterion reads as a criterion that passed, and the omission is invisible in the artifact.

criterion.description: The identifier the caller assigned to the criterion. Never minted here: a criterion the auditor named is a criterion the auditor could have invented.

state.description: `covered` a test would fail if the criterion stopped holding; `partial` a stated part is unexercised; `uncovered` nothing exercises it; `unauditable` the criterion is too ambiguous to look for, which is reported rather than resolved silently.

tests.description: Every test bearing on the criterion. Empty for `uncovered`. A test may appear under several criteria: the mapping is not one to one, and forcing it to be loses coverage.

reason.description: For `partial` and `uncovered`, what is unexercised, in the criterion's own terms. For `covered`, what the test would catch. For `unauditable`, what is ambiguous. 'No test' is not a reason; it restates the state.

notes.description: Anything a reader needs to interpret the result that no other field holds.
